approximations: Each solve is a full flop game from the scenario's preflop ranges; hands are dealt from those ranges and played to the end following GTO, recording every decision of both players, so turn and river ranges are correctly narrowed.

The flop tree is deliberately lean and depends on stack depth (flop bet 33%, raise 60% · turn bet 66%, raise 60% · river bet 75%, raise 60% · 1 raise per street · all-in when a bet commits ≥ 67% of the stack | flop bet 33%, raise 60% · turn bet 66%, raise 60% · river bet 75%, raise 60% · 1 raise per street · explicit all-in · all-in when a bet commits ≥ 67% of the stack), so the equilibrium is for that abstraction.
Solves stop near 0.75% of the flop pot; EV differences below ~0.25% of the pot are treated as ties.
No triviality filter: near-trivial decisions are kept (see spreadPot), as in real play.
EV loss is measured against a GTO opponent along GTO-sampled lines (one-step deviations), not in a full match.

criteria.allin: All-in for 92.5 bb (a raise of 318% of the pot after calling): the hero commits the whole remaining stack, making the pot 114.4 bb; the villain can only call or fold. Right with the very strongest hands, or as a bluff when the villain folds often enough.
criteria.call: Call 5.4 bb: the hero matches the villain's bet, making the pot 27.4 bb. The hero needs at least 20% equity against the villain's betting range to break even. The next board card is then dealt. Right when the hero beats enough of the villain's bluffs and thin value bets, but raising would not earn more.
criteria.fold: Fold: the hero gives up the hand, puts in no more chips and forfeits the 21.9 bb pot. Right when the hero's hand wins too rarely against the villain's betting range to justify paying 5.4 bb (it needs 20% equity).
criteria.raise_to_21_9bb: Raise to 21.9 bb: the hero puts in 21.9 bb (a raise of 60% of the pot after calling), making the pot 43.8 bb and leaving 70.6 bb behind; the villain must call 16.4 bb more, fold, or re-raise. Right with hands strong enough to get called by worse, or as a bluff with hands that block the villain's strongest holdings and do poorly when just calling.

action.instructions: You are advising the hero, the player whose turn it is, in the heads-up No-Limit Texas Hold'em spot described in the state. Pick the single legal action that maximises the hero's expected value against a strong, balanced, game-theory-optimal (GTO) opponent who cannot see the hero's cards. Weigh the hero's exact hand against the villain's likely range given the betting so far, blockers, pot odds, the stack-to-pot ratio and position. Bet and raise sizes are fixed; choose only among the listed actions.
